utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Judge Fluegge is unable to continue to sit in this case for health reasons, but most likely they will not last any longer than for the first session today, so there is a fair expectation that he would be back in the second session. Judge Moloto and myself have considered whether it would be in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case and we decided it is in the interest of justice. Having said this, the Chamber was informed that the Defence had a preliminary matter to raise. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. And good morning, Your Honours. Your Honours, we have been asked by your staff to comment on D314 in light of the Exhibit P1640, which is an excerpt of the book which comprised D314. We are satisfied that the excerpt P1640 is sufficient and thus state for the record that we withdraw D314, and all references to D314 should be understood now to relate to P1640. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Lukic, for paying attention to this request. Before we decide on the matter, I'd like to think a bit more, and the Chamber would like to think a bit more about the consequences to always have these references to be understood in a different way where there is no clue for that. So if someone would read part of the transcript, then they may have problems in finding the underlying document unless they find today's transcript where it is all explained. So whether this is the most practical way of doing that, we'll consider that, but thank you, at least, for considering the matter. And whether the withdrawal is accepted or not is still to be determined. I leave it to that at this moment. I would like to inform the parties, first of all -- but perhaps we could already ask the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom. But there is a change in the hearing schedule. In order to accommodate the scheduling of the Appeals Chamber, this Chamber will exceptionally sit on Friday the 14th of November and will not sit on Wednesday the 12th of November. So that week we have Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday, Friday as sitting days. Finally, the Prosecution has advised the Chamber that it has received the revised English translation for P6813 which was 65 ter 31407, which was MFI'd through Witness Jankovic yesterday. The revised translation has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0529-4743-ET1-1 and the court officer is hereby instructed to replace the current translation with a revised version and the Chamber admits P6813 into evidence and, as always, the Defence has an opportunity within 48 hours to further -- to revisit the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same apologies as yesterday that we continued to deal with other matters when you entered the courtroom. I would also like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday, that you are bound to speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald will now further cross-examine you. Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And if I can start with a quick apology. I should have said to Your Honours there is one matter that I have to address quickly. That is simply with regard to P61813. My friend has brought to my attention that yesterday I stated it was an order to the Rogatica Brigade command. I should have said it was an order to the Rogatica Territorial Defence command. I just wanted to put that on the record. I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby corrected and the document remains what it is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, yesterday I asked if you knew who the commander of the Kozici unit was in May 1992. You replied it may have been Spiro Pavlovski. Is it possible that the commander of the Kozici --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His last name was Paunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Yes, well, that answers my question. Thank you. If I can now move to paragraph 11 of your statement. There you state the Bosnian Serb forces never carried out organised moving of Bosnian Muslims. May I ask you what you mean by Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to members of the Territorial Defence and actually to members of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand the last part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the last part of your sentence there, Witness? The interpreters did not understand that.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I was referring to members of the Territorial Defence of Rogatica municipality, which later became VP6181 Rogatica, which stands for the Rogatica Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Are you aware of the civilian police moving the population out in an organised manner from Rogatica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no organised moving of the population in Rogatica. The Muslims had left the place for the most part prior to the war, and during the war they left with their respective units. The majority of Serbs remained in neighbourhoods like Karakaj [phoen] and Donje Polje. So either they went to live with their relatives in the neighbouring villages, but nevertheless, as I said, there was no organised moving of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P6774.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document we saw yesterday. It is a report by Rajko Kusic to the municipal assembly of Rogatica. I'm just going to read out the second paragraph. I'm sorry, I should say it's dated the 30th of November, 1992. The second paragraph states: "After sufficient number of civilian population was gathered, you have organised their transport to Sarajevo, Bijeljina, Olovo, and to Zepa, which was escorted by civilian police." And I'm going to read the last paragraph as well: "We would like to mention that you have the lists of the loyal Muslims in the area of Rogatica Municipality as well as the lists of the ones who were sent away from Rogatica in the previous months during combat activities." Witness, do you accept that certainly the civilian police were involved in the organised moving out of the civilian population of Rogatica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to repeat that in my view there was no organised moving out of Rogatica. All the individuals who reported to collection centres had an opportunity to express their desire to leave or not to leave. All those who wanted to leave, left escorted by the police for their safety. When they say here loyal, that means that those were the people who expressed their with to remain where they have always resigned and that -- resided and that means in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware that you changed your answer over the last three minutes? You explained to us that Muslims either had left the place prior to the war and during the war they left with their respective units. That's what you told us. And you said there was no organised moving out. Now confronted with this document, you add a third category which you did not include in your previous answer. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear to me. But the fact is that not all the people can leave at one time. Someone has to stay behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different matter. I just wanted to make clear to you that you changed your answer over five minutes by now admitting to a third category, whereas earlier you mentioned only two categories. If you are aware of that, I'll give an opportunity to Mr. MacDonald to continue his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'll move on to my last topic, Witness. You state in your statement in paragraph 14 that you were told to strictly adhere to the Geneva Conventions. Was it your commander Rajko Kusic who told you that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution please have P01064.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: This is a report by Rajko Kusic. It is in August 1995. And it's being sent to the command of the Drina Corps. Point 1 concerns five persons captured in Ustipraca and another person captured in Luka. I'm going to read it for you in a moment, Witness, but before I do, Rajko Kusic refers to the five persons captured as "balijas." What do you understand that term to mean?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how the Serb people refer to extremist Muslims. When I say "extremist," that means a person who does not abide by the usual standards of morale and conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: Someone who doesn't abide by the usual standards of morale and conduct. Very well, Witness. This is a daily combat report and point 1 reads: "On 7 August 1995 in the afternoon, in the canyon of the Praca River, five remaining balijas (derogatory term for the Bosnian Muslims) who were after the fall of Zepa travelling along the following route - Luka crossed the Drina river by boat - Kamenicki Potok - Babina Gora- Gradina - Kapetanovici - crossed the Drina river on the logs - Crni Vrh - Kopito above Medvedja - Ustipraca - went down to the railroad tracks at Dub and tried to reach Renovica walking on the railroad tracks were liquidated." The final paragraph under point 1, Witness, states: "The same day, in the vicinity of Luka, an unarmed Ustasha, born in Srebrenica, 24 years old, was liquidated. Before he died, he said that he fell behind the others and was looking for a food." My question, Witness: Liquidating people you've captured and questioned is not in conformity with the Geneva Conventions, is it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacDonald. Mr. Lukic, any questions in redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I have more from this morning than from the previous day, but I'll start from the end. Actually, the answer the witness gave to the question is not recorded in the transcript. So if you want to -- the question is liquidating people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think from what I remember that was translated is that the witness confirmed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that liquidating people that were captured and questioned is not in conformity with the Geneva Conventions. I think the witness confirmed that, didn't you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Jankovic, good morning once again.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read this document that has been presented to you which says that on the same date near Banja Luka an Ustasha born in Srebrenica, 24 years old, was liquidated. Judging by this document, can one deduce that this person was captured? Is that what the document shows? Or is there no reference to his being taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see here that he hadn't been captured but it also shows that these events took place in two locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- could you please clarify what event took place as we supposedly are to read in this document in two places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please answer if you can.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The canyon of the Praca river belongs to Rogatica municipality. From Mesici towards Praca and Renovici [phoen] neighbourhoods were -- or, rather, Pale, Luka, is a municipality of Srebrenica. That is outside of the zone of responsibility of the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I'm not interested mainly in the geography. Your answer was one can see here that he hadn't been captured. You're apparently talking about one person. One person, in my view, at least that's how I understand it, is linked to what happened on the same day. One unarmed Ustasha opposite to a group of five. He had been captured. But you said but it also shows that these events took place in two locations. It may be clear, Mr. Lukic, and I'm also addressing you, Mr. MacDonald, that the location of the liquidation of the five was not the same as the place of the liquidation of the one person. Is there agreement on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's how I read the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how Mr. MacDonald reads the document, that's how the Chamber reads the document. That's therefore clear. The answer was a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I think that's how the witness reads the document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He mentions there are two locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Now we do not need the exegesis of the witness for the documents, as you know, but you have -- and let me just have a look, especially where -- Witness, you said, "One can see here that he hadn't been captured." Now, that is purely explanation of a document, Mr. Lukic. Nevertheless, the witness gave it. Then I would like to know exactly what it is that makes him believe that the one person that is in the vicinity of Luka, the unarmed Ustasha, you said, was not captured. That's what you read. Where do you read that in the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I can't read because I can't see the letters on the screen. I was listening to the Prosecutor and this is how I understood things. I can't read anything that is in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was suggested to this gentleman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that this man was captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where we can read that from this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- I don't have to answer any questions. There is no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no trace in this document that he was captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was suggested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do not comment on that. The Prosecution in cross-examination can put leading questions to the witness and you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But they cannot misrepresent the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's one step too far. That is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's our position that from this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's your position --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- it's not clear whether he was just captured or he was just wounded and then found wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then asking for food, you'd say. He's about to die and then he say he was looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's your interpretation of the document. Okay. That's fine. The witness wasn't present. The way in which you want to interpret this document is -- both parties can do as they wish. Whether the witness can assist us and not having any personal knowledge of the matter is another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's why I asked him whether it's visible from this document that this man is captured where it cannot be read from this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's an interpretation of the document, Mr. Lukic, and that is what you and Mr. MacDonald and the Chamber will do itself and not to ask a witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but the -- the matter was raised and the door was opened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- for me to clarify this and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was a suggestion in the question that this is what had happened. Whether the suggestion is right or wrong is another matter. Mr. Lukic, I think that we all agree that liquidating captured people, irrespective of whether the document says so, that that is considered by the witness not to be in line with the Geneva Conventions and let's leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question to ask the witness before we proceed. Sir, sir, Mr. Witness, would the liquidation of an unarmed Ustasha be in conformity with the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, if he had been taken prisoner. If he's on the run, then anything goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do not add anything to my question. I'm asking you a simple question: Would the liquidation of an unarmed Ustasha be in conformity with the Geneva Conventions? I don't know whether he's captured or he's not captured.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view your question is ambiguous, but no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since you are criticising the question, the question is not ambiguous. A simple question: If an Ustasha is observed to be unarmed, liquidating him, would that be in conformity with the Geneva Conventions? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I insist on an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would not be in conformity with the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: And my apologies, Your Honours. It's simply a transcript matter. At temporary transcript 8 when my friend was talking about the location, he said "near Banja Luka" or that's -- sorry, that's the translation that I heard and I'm not certain what my friend said, but I presume he said "near Luka" and that it's simply a transcript matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is hereby on the record. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know, Mr. Jankovic, that Muslim fighters were taking weapons from their dead and wounded?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the course of the fighting that the Muslim forces were engaged in, do you know that the Muslims would take the weapons from those who had fallen who were either dead or wounded and those same weapons were then reused by other people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know and is it in conformity with the Geneva Conventions when one opens fire on a group of people that is firing upon you, if somebody from that group is firing upon you, do you have to check whether everybody in the group is armed or not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you don't have to check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at P2229.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were questioned about this same document yesterday. My learned friend from the Prosecutor's Office, on transcript page number 26667, suggested that this document shows that there are five centres where people in Rogatica were detained. We see that on transcript page 26667, line 8, and I'm going to quote the question first. [In English] "... he then goes on to enumerate five such centres including the former nursery-garden, the building of the malt-house factory, the building of the high school, CJB Rogatica, and the building named the rectory." [Interpretation] I will go through the document with you. Under 1, the facility referred to is the former nursery, Rasadnik. Thank you. Now we have what was said yesterday and we also have the B/C/S version of the same. CJB, which is referred to in here. I don't see anywhere where it says that people were detained there. I'm going to read a sentence where the CJB is mentioned. "During the" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. MacDonald.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I haven't posed the question yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know. But Mr. MacDonald is on his feet. I don't know for what reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honours. My friend stated that I said that this document shows there are five centres where people in Rogatica were detained. The quotation that he gives, from what I can see, I simply read the -- from the first paragraph stating there are collection centres where people of Bosniak nationality stayed. His question seems to be on the premise that I stated that people there were detained. I do not believe that I used that word, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was no mention of five in this paragraph and I have to go through each and every single one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I cut this -- could I cut this short.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's listen to the answer. The witness I think said that he was aware only of the ones he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, one or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the -- yes, one or two. That's the evidence of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether or not this document shows, and I understand your doubts, Mr. Lukic, whether this document shows that there were five, well, the witness has answered -- has given his knowledge and that's a matter of argument and debate. And I fully understand, to be quite transparent, this same thing came to my mind when the questions were asked, but whether this document shows that there were more is not for the witness to answer who says I know of only one or two. If it is misrepresentation of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's absolute misrepresentation of this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Again, this is a matter of interpreting the document. The witness has given his knowledge and he says there were only one or two, as far as he knows. And whether the document shows that there were more is not something the witness, unless you expect any specific knowledge --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please focus your question very clearly --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on the personal knowledge of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document reads, Mr. Jankovic, during that period the management structure of the SJB Rogatica consisted of Mladen Vasiljevic, the chief of the SJB, and Markic Lado [phoen], the police commander. Do you know that civilians were accommodated in the building of the police in Rogatica and that they were kept there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police station in Rogatica did not have any room to keep people there. You can still see that even today. And I claim with full responsibility that nobody was ever detained there because there was no room for such an exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It reads further on: {As read] "The Sladara building in the course of May and June 1992 was the seat of the Crisis Staff and Milorad Sokolovic held the position of the president of the aforementioned body," a man from Rogatica. This is the context within which the malt-house or Sladara is mentioned within this document. Do you know whether there were any civilians kept in the building where the seat of the Crisis Staff was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim with full responsibility that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the high school in Rogatica, the Veljko Vlahovic high school, and you said that civilians indeed stayed there. Number 5, the fifth facility that was suggested to you as a facility where civilians were kept, and you said that people were just received there and then sent to other places from there. It says in this document: [As read] "The building of the rectory, i.e. the old rectory house in the street of B. Raskovic, was functioning after a few days of the armed conflict in the area of Gracanica settlement in Rogatica most probably after the 19th of, 1992." Do you adhere to what you previously said and that's that people were not kept there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Orthodox church would not allow people to stay there, but people were received there to be safe for a while, but they did not stay for any longer time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up P6774.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a third category of people who kept on moving out after the fighting had started. Did somebody stay in Rogatica as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such people. There were girls who got married there and then for their Serbian beaus [Realtime transcript read in error "bos"].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there entire Muslim villages where people stayed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Burati, Satorovici, Zepa. Several villages in Rogatica municipality remained fully Muslim. Those were loyal Muslim villages and people expressed their wish to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now the last document, P1064.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you go to P1604. I just want to ask, sir, at page 18 line 11 to 12 you say: "There were such people. There were girls who got married there and then for their Serbian bos." I'm not quite sure I understand what "Serbian bos" are. Are you able to explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I am asking you. You may very well have been misrecorded, but if you were you can repeat your answer. But you are recorded as having said: "There were girls who got married there and then for their Serbian bos."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Their boyfriends. They had already been going out. When the war started, the girls expressed their wish to marry those lads that they had been going out with, their beaus from before, and they still lived there. They have children. They are happily married. Maybe you misunderstood me. But I'm talking about those girls who had been going out with Serbian lads before the war and decided to marry them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you so much. That explains the point there. So where you are recorded as saying "bos" you actually mean "boys." That's what you said. Thank you so much. And then, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would stay with this document for a second. [Interpretation] But this has nothing to do with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was suggested to you that that was a transport of Muslims. It says in the second paragraph, certain number of civilians from the local communities gathered and they were transported to Sarajevo, Bijeljina, Olovo, and some of them to Zepa, and that happened after a sufficient number of civilian population was gathered. You have organised their transport. Could you tell us the ethnicity of the people who were driven to Bijeljina, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that anyone was driven to Bijeljina. The people who had expressed to leave both the Serbs and the Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know. That's the answer to the question. Please proceed. Next question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just need now document P1064. And this is more for the record, Your Honours. We would inquire who translated this document because obviously the document was changed. There is a remark in the translation we do not have in the document, but it says: "Derogatory term for the Bosnian Muslims." So if this is done by the Prosecution, we would kindly ask for this document just draft translation to be sent to the CLSS and for this remark to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have dealt with the matter of explanation of certain terms. Is it -- let's try to have matters straight. Irrespective of whether it should be -- this explanation should be in the translation, yes or no, sometimes you know that the linguistical explanation is given for terms which are not directly -- which cannot be directly translated into another language, so therefore the original word remains and then it's explained what that word means. That happens now and then. I think we have dealt with the matter before. But before verifying what our solution was at the time, is there a dispute, is "balijas" -- is that not a derogatory term for Bosnian Muslims? That's my question, Mr. Lukic. Is that the Defence's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to say that -- and I come from Bosnia. I have to say that many people understand this term in a different ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. You say there is not one --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is not one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- uniform understanding of this word.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that Muslims would call another Muslims "balijas."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That doesn't mean that it's not derogatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It does not but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have heard similar --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It really can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- have several meanings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question, of course, is then what is the prevailing meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we have heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it to that. And I have heard that the position of the Defence, which does not depend on where you come from, but is a position taken by the Defence, could by anyone, that the Defence's position is that this is -- the term "balijas" is understood in different ways by different persons. We'll verify again what we did in previous instances because it's not the first time that the matter arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's all I had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- for this witness. I just wanted to thank him in our language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jankovic, thank you for answering our questions and I have no further questions for you. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Before I give you an opportunity -- would you have any further questions, Mr. MacDonald?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. I would have one quick remark to make, if I could. And simply that the word "misrepresent" is quite strong in my home jurisdiction, and I would just like to say I don't believe I did misrepresented any evidence. If I did, my sincere apologies to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a conditional apology. Let's not bother the witness with that at this very moment. Witness, I have one matter which is still not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you told us that you were called approximately the 20th of April to the TO and within a few days you witnessed the distribution of arms. You also told us that on the 20th of May you became a member of the VRS. In paragraph 4 of your statement, you told us that the distribution of arms, so the arming organised by the Territorial Defence, lasted two to three months. What then approximately is the starting point in terms of time? Did it start before you were called on the 20th of April? Did it start at that time? Did it start two or three months before you joined the VRS? Could you be a bit more precise even without knowing exact dates but linking it to certain events when these two or three months of arming took place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement I said, and it can be checked, that I did not remember the exact date when I joined the VRS. However, yesterday I said that in the certificate that I received it states that I was a member of the VRS from the 20th of May 1996 [as interpreted]. So when all the work stopped on the 20th of April, that's when the arming started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your reference to 1996, I suppose, should be the 20th of May, 1992. Perhaps that's a transcript error.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, it's a wrong date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say arming started on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean that there was no arming in March; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only soldiers who were mobilised had weapons and they were waiting to be dispatched to a unit in Han Pijesak according to their assignments and also people who had some personal weapons. I don't know that there was any arming of the population prior to that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From who were these weapons received?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was issued by the Territorial Defence. I don't know exactly how it was distributed, but I think that it was the weapons at the disposal of the Rogatica TO. I am not quite sure but I believe that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But from whom did the Rogatica TO receive those weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said following the distribution of weapons that had existed in Rogatica municipality in the joint TO and the joint police station, the reserve personnel also had some weapons with them. So this part of the TO weapons, this arsenal, I don't know how it was distributed, I never inquired where the weapons had come from but I think they came from the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what then exactly does the sentence mean: "I was called when some of the weapons were received"? If you say it was the TO, you were the TO, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The weapons were not distributed in the town but rather people who were in charge of taking over the weapons were called to come to certain check-points. That was myself and Milos Jankovic, a cousin of mine, were among those people. We received weapons at the point in Pljesevica, and, as I said, we also gave weapons to the people whom we trusted and believed that they would not abuse it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And those were people not at check-points. In what position were those people exactly, people you trusted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the people who were good heads of household, who were not prone to misuse of alcohol, who had no problems, mental or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But in what positions were they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. They were along the defence lines in the Pljesevica village. That's where they were deployed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But were they TO members as well or were they unorganised or ...?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We organised people in order to protect ourselves. I did not know their disposition. I supposed that a number of them were members of the TO as per establishment. After serving in the army I became a member of the TO, and Meho Agic was my direct superior until the split took place. So I don't know all the people who were there, but I know that they were deployed along the defence lines of the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say you distributed arms to persons of which you did not know whether they were members of the TO but just because they were defending their village lines, is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I claim that at that point in time we were all the TO because the war had already started. We did not join any of the military units but rather placed ourselves at the disposal of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you didn't know whether they were TO members but you considered everyone to be available to support TO activities?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that mean that good house fathers, that the whole community in order to defend their villages were provided with weapons unless they were known to be irresponsible persons?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking about the very beginning. These were small quantities of weapons and people who were going to receive them were selected. The weapons were to be left there according to the law so that others can use them. It wasn't that a person could keep a weapon with themselves unendingly. Once we set up a brigade, that's when larger quantities of weapons started to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May or June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now if you say this distribution of weapons lasted for two or three months and that apparently is not the same distribution of weapons as happened in May and June, this brings me back to March, April, perhaps even late February. Do you have any comment on my understanding of the chronology?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before March and February, a certain number of weapons were distributed to the reserve police force in the villages and also it was given to people who were mobilised and who were also deployed in villages. But I claim with full responsibility that the first weapons received from the TO, Rajko Kusic personally distributed the weapons to us, and I think that they had come from the initial quantities, the small quantities that arrived from the TO. Later on, the weapons were collected at Borike. I don't know where it came from. That was sometime in June. And at Borike, the weapons were given to the people. So I cannot say that the people were all armed on the 20th April. Those were only small quantities at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you understand to be small quantities?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to 20 pieces of weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Twenty pieces of weapons for the whole of the population under which they were distributed or for a village?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for my village of Pljesevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which had how many inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pljesevica has 130 households, times four, let's say about 500 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. You wanted to make an observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACDONALD
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. It was just about the word "misrepresent."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It was about misrepresentation. Sorry that I had not ... Mr. Lukic, no further questions, I understand. Mr. Jankovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you very much for having coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Have a good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although we should take a break now, the Chamber was informed that there was a matter to be raised in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if that matter has any impact on how we will proceed after the break, perhaps it's better to know it now. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think it may make sense to proceed now rather than after the break on this quick preliminary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's a matter of minutes?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Since we went on longer than usual, we'll take a slightly longer break of 25 minutes, so we'll resume at 10 minutes past 11.00, but I already announce now that in order to make protective measures effective that we'll start in closed session at 10 minutes past 11.00 and then soon after that, once the witness has taken the stand, we'll move into open session again. We take a break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness GRM277, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D05231 from 65 ter list. The document should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're invited to come a bit closer to the microphone. Perhaps the usher could assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the document. Don't read it aloud. Just look at it and tell us whether the information contained in the document is accurate and correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5231 receives number D684, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D684 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I have a few questions for you, Madam. Did you give a statement to the Mladic Defence in a written form?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up 1D01657. Again, the document should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what you see before you, is this your signature? Is the information on this page accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we look at the last page of the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The same question, Madam. Is this your signature and did you enter the date in your own hand?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a few questions for you. Can we zoom in on paragraph 3 in your statement. Can you tell the Trial Chamber while you were being proofed for today's testimony, did you tell me that something should be changed in paragraph 3? We are talking about a semantic change. In the last sentence behind the words "that guarded two buildings," instead of the words "the neighbourhood was a Muslim cemetery" should be replaced who -- "which were in the Muslim cemetery"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, could you please look at paragraph 6. Did you tell me that in the last sentence of this paragraph where it says, and I quote, "where Serbs were taken," these words should be replaced "and Serbs were taken to the correctional facility"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, to be able to understand the sentence better, could you please read the entire sentence in the new version?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The new sentence should read: "At that time the medical centre and the correctional facility were under Muslim control and Serbs were taken to the correctional facility."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 10, did you suggest that in the penultimate sentence the words, and I quote, "I remember that" should be eliminated and replaced by the following words at the end, after the comma, the word "office" should be replaced, and I quote "of this unit which was headquartered in the hotel."

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, I would like to read the newly-worded sentence: "During that time, there was a duty office of this unit which was headquartered in the hotel." Would that be true to what you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please clarify if the remainder of that sentence still stands which reads: "... I know that orders came from the Foca Territorial Defence Staff." Is that still part of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I know but I will ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The remainder of the witness after the comma where it says, "... I know that orders came from the Foca Territorial Defence Staff," would those words remain as part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, Witness, that we have made these corrections, as you're sitting today in this courtroom and after having taken the solemn declaration to speak the truth about the events, would you adhere to the answers provided in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave I would like to tender this 65 ter document 1D01657 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1657 receives number D685, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, nevertheless I would have one or two questions for the witness in this context. You said the duty office was located in the hotel. Which hotel are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the hotel in Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. There is one hotel in Foca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now my next question would be you corrected now. When you signed it, did you not notice that, these shortcomings in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember but I believe that I noticed the same thing at the time. There is just one hotel in Foca and there was just one office in that hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But when you signed the document which, if I understand well was in June of this year, a couple of months after you were interviewed, when you signed it, did you make any -- did you note at that time or did you inform those who had interviewed you or took your signature that there was still corrections to be made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so but maybe I skimmed through the document too fast. That may be my own mistake, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you given sufficient time to read through it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any further questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, perhaps this would be a good moment for me to read a summary of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness GRM277 is a nurse by education. When the war started in Foca, she was a member of the medical personnel at the department of internal medicine of the Foca medical centre. On the eve of the breakout of the conflicts in Foca, the situation in hospital was more or less normal but the witness realised that already March 1992 some of the colleagues had started sending their children away, both Serbs and Muslims. At the beginning of April 1992 when fighting started in Foca, she was invited to come to work so she managed to get to the hospital under fire. She stayed in the hospital for the next fortnight and she noticed that only Muslim patients came to the hospital as well as women and children who were not sick but they were looking for a safe haven because of all the fighting that was already going on in town. Once the blockade was lifted of this facility and when the Serb forces took over control of the hospital, the Muslim population that was there and wanted to leave the town was allowed to leave Foca with their families in their cars or in any other means of transportation available to them. During the night before the hospital and the correctional facility were deblocked, the Muslims who were in the hospital and who controlled the correctional facility fled from those two facilities. During that period, the witness also worked in the infirmary that was organised by the Territorial Defence of Foca. And she provided care to the Dragan Nikolic unit. She personally knows that at the time this unit received orders from the TO Foca staff. Those orders were verbal. And finally, the witness eye-witnessed the unlawful activities of individuals who had arrived from Montenegro and who were warned to leave the territory of Foca municipality. The witness inferred from that that there were renegade individuals at the time. Thank you. This is a short summary of the witness's statement, and with your leave, Your Honours, I would like to put several questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up D685. The document should not be broadcast. I'm interested in paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. D685, I had not mentioned but now add, so that it's clear on the record, that it was admitted under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell the Court what your duties were? What did you do for the Dragan Nikolic unit? First of all, when were you attached to provide medical assistance to the members of this unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the moment the blockade was lifted off the hospital, we could leave the hospital. There was no personnel in any of the infirmaries. I would go to the outpatients clinic and to the Dragan Nikolic unit and I would still be on duty at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you went to the Dragan Nikolic unit, where did you actually go? Where did you assist the Dragan Nikolic unit members?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever needed. I don't know what you mean. I went on house calls, or in the office, in the field, wherever needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you administered medical assistance to the members of this unit in the field.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you joined this unit and went to the places where they were engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Until when did you -- provided medical assistance to this unit members?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, when you say "until the very end," what do you mean? Until when?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For as long as needed because that unit stopped existing at one point in time. There were very few men in that unit. When that unit was disbanded, I can't tell you. I don't know when it stopped existing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your work that you described, did you ever receive any orders or instructions from superior officers in any form of exercises, discrimination against the sick or the wounded based on their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you were doing your job, and I mean both within the hospital and with the unit, did you notice any unlawful or inhumane treatment of the members of the units that you provided medical care for?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. We have no further questions for you at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Ms. Bibles, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness GRM277, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Bibles. Ms. Bibles, and you'll find her to your right, is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: First, I have some questions about medical institutions in Foca municipality. Before the war, is it accurate to say that there was both a hospital and a medical centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And a medical centre?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm looking at paragraph 6 of your statement where you talk about the medical centre. I was trying to ascertain whether that is a different place than the hospital in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then you've testified that Serb units secured the Foca hospital. Do you believe that was around the 7 April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I can tell you that the Chamber has received evidence quite recently from an individual named Miladin Gagovic that there were Serb units securing the hospital as early as 7 April 1992. Does that assist in your recollections as to when these Serb units secured the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, you did put to the witness that the Serb units secured the Foca hospital. Reading paragraph 8, it is about lifting a blockade which I have some difficulties in reconciling with securing. But I must admit that there is no time-frame there as there is not in most of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that's part of what I was trying to reconcile as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And perhaps if we could -- well, I'll actually move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At some point during that time-frame, April-May 1992, were you mobilised to provide medical assistance to the Dragan Nikolic unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, when the war started, I was working at the hospital -- actually, I was to be on the night shift. A car was sent to fetch me because there was no movement around the time -- the night. We stayed there for 10 or 15 days because the hospital was blocked. Only the ambulance went to the town. The only information we received was over Radio Sarajevo. We didn't even get any food supplies.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Ma'am, I perhaps was not clear enough. At some point were you mobilised to provide medical assistance to the Dragan Nikolic unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At any point. Let's start there.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you personally mobilised either before or during the war to provide medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the war. But not before the war. This unit did not even exist at the time, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, I do have a few brief questions about your work with the Dragan Nikolic unit which you mention in paragraphs 10 and 11 of your statement. Now, is it correct that this was a military unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first month it was not a military unit. It was not the army. These were self-organised groups, to the best of my knowledge. I went there only when and if needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When and if needed, is that prior to them -- the unit becoming part of the military?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's the end of April, beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So after they became part of the military, is that when you were mobilised and became -- and started working with this unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, these units that were there, when certain structure came into place in June or July, those were not proper units. Those were just self-organised groups of, let's say, some younger men, and this particular Dragan Nikolic unit only had one room in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And by the way, was this the hotel, is it Zelengora?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Going back to the Dragan Nikolic unit, did you have a good relationship with the members of that unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say so while I was working in the field and being with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I would like to go through some names and ask you whether they were members of this unit. Did you know Radomir Kovac and was he a member of this unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Dragan Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member on and off. He was not a permanent member of the unit. He used to come and go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Zoran Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And Jagos Kostic, was he also a member?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing with him. He was not a permanent member. He would just come and go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But at some point he was a member of this unit and he worked with Radomir Kovac while he was with the unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "he worked." I knew these guys whilst they were in the field and when they needed my assistance and this man that you mentioned, Kovac, he would just occasionally come to the unit and I don't know what his duties were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When he was with the unit, you would agree that he worked with Radomir Kovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both with Radomir Kovac and everybody else. I don't know what other kind of co-operation you can have in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That answers my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but, Ms. Bibles, there is -- "when he was with the unit," the last person the witness referred to was Kovac, although in your question, originally, it was Kostic. Did you see Kostic and Kovac together in that unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were all together. There was no separation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning back to Radomir Kovac, did you meet him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the parties to assist me. Did I hear the witness say "they were all together" or "we were all together"? I think I heard "they were all together." When you said there was no separation, did you say "they were all together" or did you say "we were all together"? Just repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was there, and that's the only time that I can speak of, when I was in the field. I cannot tell you anything about what happened in the field when I was away, whether they were together or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you referred to them being together, not there being no separation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there was no separation. Nobody stood out individually as being closer to one individual and less close to another. You know how it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I leave it to that. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning back to Radomir Kovac, did you meet him at the garrison clinic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, when we say "garrison," at the beginning of the war in April of 1992 you're referring to the Foca Territorial Defence garrison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Where specifically was the clinic located?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time when war started in Foca municipality, I don't know how familiar you are with the town, the hospital is outside of the town. You have to pass by the KP facility on the way to the hospital, and together with the medical clinic this area was populated by Muslims, and initially they considered that to be theirs. And at that time only Muslims were admitted to the hospital, specifically women and children. During that time we didn't even have enough food. After that the Foca Territorial Defence organised themselves outside of Foca, and in a restaurant outside of Foca they set up an infirmary for the wounded members of the Serbian community.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would like to follow-up on that, then. After the hospital came within Serb control, where did the infirmary for these units, the military units, go to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people, the local residents.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When you talk about -- when we were talking about the garrison clinic, where was that located after it left the initial, I believe you called it, a restaurant or cafe? Where did it go after that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They remained for a lengthy period of time there, then the medical clinic was liberated and it started operating as a proper medical clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And going back to the beginning of the war in April when you first met the unit, did they wear olive-drab SNB uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to go to 65 ter 31446 [Realtime transcript read in error "13446"] please. And we'll be looking at page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friend, but the answer in line 4, page 48, I didn't hear clearly and I'm afraid that this does not reflect the answer. If it could be -- please be repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I -- you were asked and there is some doubt as to what exactly your answer was. You were asked: "Going back to the beginning of the war in April when you first met the unit, did they wear olive-drab SNB uniforms?" What was your answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's what the transcript tells us, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, what was the number of the 65 ter number you asked for?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's written 13 on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction, Your Honour. If we could go to 31446, page 9, please. And not for broadcast, I'm sorry. Although I believe this may have been an open session, but we'll err on the side of caution for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Witness, we have in front of us your testimony from your -- the previous case in which you were here, and I'd like to start reading at page -- excuse me, at line 2 you were asked about Radomir Kovac: "Q. Since you saw him during the war, what did he wear at the time?" Your answer: "During the first days, he wore that SNB uniform, a green one. Everybody wore that. And only after a longer period of time -- I cannot tell you exactly how long this was, but this was in the beginning. After that they got some kind of camouflage uniforms that they wore out in the field." Does this refresh your recollection as to the uniforms worn by the members of this unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority -- but now whether someone due to indigence put on the SNB uniform or where they had acquired it from -- but the majority of these young men were dressed in civilian clothes, in blue jeans and jackets. Now, as for what I said here, I don't know if -- well, you know that up until August even they used to wear their civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you stand by your testimony from before that at some point, and I believe you've just said at least by August of 1992, they had some kind of camouflage uniforms that they wore in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you stand by your testimony from before that at some point, and I believe you've just said at least by August of 1992, they had some kind of camouflage uniforms that they wore in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: Everybody purchased and what was affordable to them. They just found a way around it. I myself didn't have a uniform almost ever.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So I guess I'm not clear, are you modifying the answer that you gave before?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not modifying it. What am I modifying? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Witness, it's a bit -- the testimony in the other case was read to you in which you are referring to the period after the beginning, and you said: "After that they got some kind of camouflage uniforms that they wore out in the field." Now you say that everyone bought what was affordable, but at that time you said they got uniforms and that's what they wore. Are you changing that at this moment or are you still standing by that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I don't know if you understand me. You know, there was no issuing of uniforms. For example, I received the first uniform as late as in September because nobody gave me one before that, and where these people got hold of uniforms, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether they paid for it, whether they -- where they got it, from whom they got it, but they had those uniforms on from August and they were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- wearing -- well, in your testimony you said, "After that they got some kind of camouflage uniforms that they wore out in the field," which suggests that you saw them wearing those uniforms.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I don't know the source of the uniforms, how they acquired them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one asked you for that. We are just interested in hearing from you what you saw and what you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Similarly, I put it to you that when talking about the beginning in your previous statement you were talking about during the first days that they were wearing SNB uniforms, a green one, everybody wore that, whereas now you tell us that in the beginning they were wearing civilian clothes or at least some or many of them which, of course, is not the same. If you say everybody wore that uniform, that means they were not in civilian dress. I just want to draw your attention to the fact that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then most probably at that time maybe I was nervous and didn't understand the question properly. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this question at that time simply was "what did he wear at the time," apparently talking about Kovac, and then you added yourself, after having described the uniform he was dressed in, that everybody wore that. So you hardly can be -- have been confused by that question because it was something you added yourself spontaneously. I just draw your attention to the fact that the testimony as we read it from the transcript is not fully consistent with what you're telling us now. Ms. Bibles, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I wanted to go back to something that you've said in this discussion, and I believe you said: "I received the first uniform as late as September ..." Did you receive a camouflage uniform in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is your answer yes you received a camouflage uniform in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JANKOVIC [Resumed]
